intent_snapshot.goal: Make imm-run the only phase that stops the user at entry: a model Skill call for imm-planner or imm-brainstorm no longer revokes the session's run entry, and the revision_owner_required edit guard is deleted on Claude Code and Pi together with its source, tests and contract text.

acceptance.assertion: Meet T1, D2 and invariants I1 and I2 in docs/specs/run-only-gates.spec.md: PhaseEntryState carries run_live only; the imm-planner and imm-brainstorm Skills are admitted for a fresh, live and unreadable state; the imm-run Skill, enroll and start_unattended_batch are refused without a live literal-user run entry; a literal plan entry revokes and a later literal run entry restores; legacy log lines still reduce and a malformed line is unreadable.

Meet D1 and BR-SCN-1 on Claude Code: after a literal run entry, a model Skill call for imm-planner or imm-brainstorm returns no decision and leaves the phase-entry store byte-identical, with or without an active claim, and enroll is then admitted without a fresh /imm-run. Without a run entry enroll is still denied run_entry_required, and a literal /imm-planner prompt still revokes the run entry.

Meet D3, I3 and BR-SCN-5 on both Hosts: with a plan entry as the session's latest entry and an active Managed claim, a file-edit tool call inside the active scope is allowed on Claude Code and on Pi, and no code path emits revision_owner_required. The Lane guard still denies an edit outside a batch Lane and the Pi tool gate for enroll and start_unattended_batch is unchanged.

Meet D3, D4 and BR-7: runtime/assurance/revision_owner.ts, tests/revision-owner-guard.test.ts and tests/revision-owner-contract.test.ts are deleted; the BASELINE, Planner and Loop contracts no longer say that a model-entered Planner ends the run entry or that a plan-entry session may not edit in-scope files; the three BASELINE copies are identical; ADR 0022 records the decision and what it supersedes; the packaged Claude bundle matches its source.

advisory_findings.summary: Store byte-identity is asserted only without an active claim; the with-claim test (SCN-5) asserts that the run entry stays live and enroll is admitted, not that the store bytes are unchanged. The code returns before any store or claim read, so both cases take one path and the behaviour holds; only the with-claim half of 'byte-identical, with or without an active claim' lacks a direct assertion.

evidence.trigger: Literal run entry, then claimWorkspace(cwd, 'task-a'), then a model Skill call for imm-planner: the test compares no storeBytes snapshot in this case, so a future claim-dependent write to the entry store that keeps run_live true would not be caught.
